nodes.community_name: cTrader CLI Backtest and Optimize Research
nodes.rationale: Measured throughput improves through multiple processes, but memory use and CPU saturation justify a conservative default below the observed saturation point and benchmark-based increases.

nodes.label: Live Network Backtest Non-Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Network resources accessed during backtesting return their current state rather than a historical state synchronized with simulated time, so direct Redis reads would undermine reproducibility.

nodes.label: Python Redis-to-CSV Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshotting Redis through Python into an immutable CSV retains the existing cBot contract, avoids raw-socket and package-loading risks, and makes past runs reproducible.

nodes.label: ArchivedRuns Preservation Protocol
nodes.rationale: cTrader overwrites the Backtesting directory, so each verified run must be copied before another run starts to preserve comparable raw evidence.

nodes.label: Record MD Handoff Protocol
nodes.rationale: Maintains continuity between Claude and Codex by updating current state, open work, and a newest-first handoff entry whenever the user requests record md.

nodes.label: Completed-Run-Only Ingestion
nodes.rationale: Failed, cancelled, timed-out, or interrupted runs must leave no SQL rows, while their file artifacts remain available for diagnosis.

nodes.label: Do Not Store Derivable Columns
nodes.rationale: Values reproducible from retained columns or tables are calculated in queries instead of duplicated, reducing the schema from 117 to 83 columns.

nodes.label: Shared Database Migration Safety

nodes.label: Single File-to-Payload-to-SQL Extraction Path

nodes.label: CLI Default Backend Decision
nodes.rationale: The CLI pipeline remains the default because measured plugin and CLI results and speed were equivalent while the CLI path supplied stronger validation, timeout, logging, retry, resume, and provenance controls.

nodes.label: Shared Core with Executor Backends
nodes.rationale: Planning, scheduling, storage, retries, and normalized results belong in one core while CLI and Plugin API remain replaceable executor backends and the bridge remains transport-only.

nodes.label: Concurrency versus Accumulated Simulated Activity
nodes.rationale: Concurrent process risk and accumulated simulated-trade volume are distinct mechanisms and must not be conflated when explaining account or platform limits.

nodes.label: CLI Operational Safety Controls
nodes.rationale: Retries, progress-aware watchdogs, report-first success classification, credential redaction, version probing, claim recovery, and PID-scoped termination address distinct observed failure modes without killing unrelated workers.

nodes.label: Selection Objective Alignment
nodes.rationale: DSR and PBO must evaluate the same objective used by the actual selection process; otherwise they measure a different winner and cannot validate the implemented decision rule.

nodes.label: Independent Walk-Forward and DSR/PBO Branches
nodes.rationale: Walk-forward and DSR/PBO answer complementary questions from the same original grid, so they run independently rather than nesting one inside the other and introducing avoidable cost or look-ahead.

nodes.label: Small-Sample Tail-Risk Method Comparison
nodes.rationale: For short histories, moving and stationary variants are reported alongside non-overlapping bootstrap because the simpler fixed partition materially understated measured breach risk in the observed sample.

nodes.label: Dual-Series Monte Carlo Model
nodes.rationale: End-of-day balance returns and intraday minimum-equity drawdowns serve different statistical purposes, so paired daily series are resampled together rather than forcing one field to represent both compounding and breach detection.

nodes.label: Preregistered Experiment Contract
nodes.rationale: Data zones, parameter space, selection rules, trial budget, and holdout access are locked before execution so research decisions cannot be revised after observing results.

nodes.label: CQRS Dash Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Read-only dashboard queries are separated from command triggers, while Dash background callbacks use separate processes and periodic refreshes to keep long-running jobs responsive.

nodes.label: Manual Final-Stage Selection
nodes.rationale: The final parameter choice remains an explicit human judgment after reviewing grid and walk-forward evidence, rather than an undocumented automatic best-candidate rule.

nodes.label: Inclusive End-Date Signal Hashing
nodes.rationale: cTrader executes the full requested end day, so signals from that day must participate in the run identity hash.

nodes.label: Walk-Forward as Labeled Backtests
nodes.rationale: Walk-forward and optimization use the same backtest mechanism, so walk-forward differences are represented as labels and a self-reference rather than a separate decision table.
